Rescue good food.

A surplus-food marketplace designed around trust, store efficiency and visible donations in Berlin.

Project overview

Good food deserves a future.

The opportunity: make surplus food easier to rescue and harder to waste.

01

The problem

Shoppers want affordable surplus food but cannot always judge bag contents, pickup windows or what happens to leftovers.

02

The operational challenge

Store staff need a surplus routine that fits into existing shifts, rather than another manual process.

03

The product decision

Prioritise trust before growth: transparent offers, clear handovers and a visible donation journey.

FairShare | Anu Jose | Product Management02 / 08
Discovery & research

Trust is the barrier to rescue.

Qualitative research and tester feedback informed three product decisions.

01

Unknown contents

Show exact or likely contents, photos and household fit to reduce uncertainty.

02

Unclear deadlines

Show pickup and cancellation times separately and repeat them at checkout.

03

Invisible outcomes

Simplify sell-or-donate decisions and show donation status.

“It feels bad, like you throw money away.”Shopper interview
“If it’s safe but not pretty, we try to donate it.”Store owner interview

Product experience / Shopper

A focused consumer journey from nearby discovery to a confirmed pickup.

Product experience / Store & charity

Make the food journey visible.

FairShare | Anu Jose | Product Management05 / 08
Strategy & prioritisation

Start narrow. Prove the loop.

Proposed pilot: Prenzlauer Berg, five store types and three charity partners.

NOW

Trust & checkout

Account entry, discovery, exact or likely contents, separate deadlines and reservation confirmation.

NEXT

Close the handover

Store surplus, sell-or-donate decisions, pickup codes, cancellation and donation tracking.

LATER

Production readiness

Real payments, stock integrations, charity notifications, push alerts, German localisation and server accounts.

Measurement & validation

Measure trust, efficiency and impact.

Six proposed pilot success signals. These are targets, not achieved results.

>85%

Pickup completion

Reservations that result in collection.

<5%

Missed pickups

Validate clear deadlines and reminders.

>50%

Exact-content listings

Share of offers with known contents.

<30 s

Staff time per item

Test fit with existing store workflow.

Weekly

Donations per store

Track kilograms donated and delivered.

>30%

Food journey opens

Share of active shoppers exploring it.

FairShare | Anu Jose | Product Management07 / 08
Reflection & next steps

From product concept to interactive experience.

FairShare demonstrates how discovery, product strategy and delivery planning can connect.

Delivered

Vision and strategy, research-led requirements, shopper and store wireframes, user flows, interactive prototype, landing page and Jira-ready backlog.

What still needs validation

Test whether clearer offer information improves pickup completion, whether staff can handle surplus within the time target, and whether charity handovers are reliable.

Prototype boundary

Browser-based demonstration with simulated payments, stock sync, notifications and charity status. No live transactions or verified operational impact.
